# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have found no tactile clues. Read the manual and coordinate with Deaf using gestures. Have Deaf report the display, light, and each wire's visible colour or marking through a gesture code you establish, then tell me which wire position must be cut and any required light or display condition.

I will establish a legal five-value code using one through five fingers: ☝, ✌, 🤟, 🖖, 🖐. 🤝 separates entries. The manual is then sent as input/output pairs in the listed colour order: blue→blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green. Deaf should use this code to understand the required mapping, inspect all visual information, and verbally relay it to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟","🖖","🖐","🤝","☝","☝","🤝","✌","🖖","🤝","🤟","🖐","🤝","🖖","🤟","🤝","🖐","✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👇","👉"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb view: display reads 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires by position: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.
Blind says to Mute: I have display 0, blue indicator, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue from the incoming report. Please read the manual and tell me the exact safe wire position to cut, including any display or light condition.

The blue indicator requires cutting the blue wire. Among the reported wires, only position 5 is blue. No display condition is specified by the manual, so the display reading 0 does not alter the instruction. Deaf must relay “cut wire 5; indicator blue” to Blind by voice.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","🤝","☝","🤝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your five gestures are reported as open hand, handshake, raised index, handshake, raised index, but their meaning is unclear. Please send Deaf an explicit code: use a hand sign directly meaning the wire number 1 through 5, and use handshake only as a separator. Then send any required display digit and light condition in the same clear format so Deaf can state the exact cut.

I will use conventional finger-count signs directly for wire positions: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5. I will use 👊 for display digit 0. For the light, I will use the manual’s colour order, so ☝ means blue; Deaf can also verify the actual blue indicator visually. The required information is wire 5, display 0, blue light. Handshakes separate fields only.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🤝","✌","🤝","🤟","🤝","🖖","🤝","🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","🤝","👊","🤝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not encode this through gestures. Speak the manual rule and the exact computed safe wire position directly to me, using plain words and numbers. Include how display 0 and blue light affect the decision.

I cannot speak or send anything directly to Blind because I am Mute; my only outgoing channel is gestures to Deaf. The rule is: with a blue light, cut the blue wire. Display 0 has no effect because the manual gives no display-dependent rule. Since wire 5 is blue, the exact position is 5. I will signal Deaf to state this plainly to Blind on Deaf’s next speaking turn.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","🤝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this exact code for the current state display 0 and blue light. Send one gesture for the safe wire: index-up means wire 1, victory means wire 2, three-finger gesture means wire 3, four-finger gesture means wire 4, raised open hand means wire 5. Then send handshake as separator, then thumbs-up means cut now and thumbs-down means do not cut. Send only that sequence.

The manual maps blue light to the blue wire, and the blue wire is position 5. Display 0 has no effect because the manual gives no display rule. I will send exactly the requested wire-five, separator, and cut-now gesture sequence to Deaf, who can relay it to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","🤝","👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous wire was correctly cut, but the bomb has changed and no new display, light, or wire arrangement is available yet. I cannot inspect it or speak to Blind; Deaf must obtain and report the new visual state. I will not send an ambiguous gesture that could be mistaken for an instruction.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut confirmed. New bomb state: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut.
Blind says to Mute: For the new state display 0 and yellow light, use the established code: index-up wire 1, victory wire 2, three-finger gesture wire 3, four-finger gesture wire 4, raised open hand wire 5; handshake separator; thumbs-up means cut now and thumbs-down means do not cut. Send the manual's exact next instruction.

The yellow light requires cutting the green wire. The green wire is position 2; display 0 does not affect the manual rule. I will send the exact requested sequence for wire 2 and cut now.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","🤝","👍"])
```
